items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: in the early days of like John Kirby where he did play some four-beat on the tuba... John Kirby did for a while

ctx.x: Do you think that — this is an awful general question — when music moved from sort of two-beat into four-beat, how much was the string bass a role in that?

Well you know I hear people phrasing in four, at least the horn, even with the two-beat feel going on. But I think when the musicians eventually got the idea and the feel of the pulsing four-beat they really didn’t want to go back. And so the tuba can do that and in the early days of like John Kirby where he did play some four-beat on the tuba, it was too unwieldy. And so once the string bass got ahold of that sound, and it was time for a change. You know jazz is always evolving, and putting the banjo away and…
Here’s a question that rarely works, okay? What was the worst gig you’ve ever played?
